terms.comment: A description of ours: expers with the genitive, “having no share in”, and glūten, classically glue, in the sense Morgan–Owens gives it, the sticky part of wheat (after Mattioli’s glūtinum ex similāgine). No reference work we searched (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini) has a word for gluten-free. Expers is used rather than a phrase with sine, which in Latin does not readily stand as an adjective.
The plain phrase, after a verb: pānem sine glūtine quaerimus.

phrases.latin: Glūten eī nocet; pānem sine glūtine quaerimus.
phrases.english: He can’t have gluten; we’re looking for gluten-free bread.

sources: Lewis & Short: gluten · Lewis & Short: expers
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. gluten.
